lessons.title: The topic marker は
lessons.summary: は tells the listener what the sentence is about. As a particle it is pronounced わ.

examples.reading: わたし は がくせい です。

questions.prompt: Which particle marks ‘I’ as the topic?
questions.explanation: は marks 私 as the topic: ‘As for me, I am a student.’
今日は means ‘as for today’. Remember that particle は is pronounced わ.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means ‘As for this book, it is interesting’?
questions.explanation: この本 is the topic, so は follows it.

lessons.title: The subject marker が
lessons.summary: が identifies the grammatical subject, often introducing new information or answering ‘who?’ and ‘what?’.

examples.reading: ねこ が います。

questions.prompt: Which particle identifies the thing that exists?
questions.explanation: 猫 is the subject of います, so it takes が.

questions.prompt: Which answer naturally responds to ‘Who came?’
questions.explanation: が highlights 田中さん as the answer to ‘who?’
Rain is what is falling, so 雨 is marked by が.

lessons.title: The object marker を
lessons.summary: を marks the direct object affected by an action. As a particle it is pronounced お.

examples.reading: みず を のみます。

questions.prompt: Which particle marks what is being eaten?
questions.explanation: パン receives the action of eating, so it is the direct object.
音楽 is the object of 聞きます.
The book is what you read, so use を.

lessons.title: Destination and time に
lessons.summary: に marks a destination, a point in time, or the target of an action.

examples.japanese: 七時に学校に行きます。
examples.reading: しちじ に がっこう に いきます。
examples.english: I go to school at seven.

questions.explanation: 学校 is the destination of 行きます.

questions.prompt: Which particle marks a specific time?
questions.explanation: A precise time normally takes に.

questions.prompt: What does the first に mark?
questions.explanation: 友達 is the target or recipient of giving.

lessons.title: Action location and means で
lessons.summary: で marks where an action happens or the means used to perform it.

examples.japanese: 電車で東京へ行きます。
examples.reading: でんしゃ で とうきょう へ いきます。
examples.english: I go to Tokyo by train.

questions.prompt: Which particle marks where studying happens?
questions.explanation: Studying is an action performed at the library, so use で.
で can mark the tool or means used for an action.
The action 遊びます occurs in the park, so use で.

lessons.title: Connection and possession の
lessons.summary: の connects nouns. It often corresponds to possession or ‘of’ in English.

examples.reading: これ は せんせい の ほん です。

questions.prompt: Which particle shows that the bag belongs to Mika?
questions.explanation: ミカのかばん means ‘Mika’s bag’.

choices: A Japanese film / film of Japan
questions.answer: A Japanese film / film of Japan
questions.explanation: の connects Japan with the film and describes its origin/type.
の connects 私 and 友達: ‘my friend’.

lessons.title: Adding with も
lessons.summary: も replaces は, が or を to mean ‘also’, ‘too’ or sometimes ‘even’.

examples.reading: わたし も いきます。

questions.explanation: 妹も means ‘my younger sister too’.
も adds this item to something already mentioned.
も replaces the subject/topic marker to mean ‘Ken too’.

lessons.title: And, with and quotations と
lessons.summary: と joins nouns, marks a companion, and marks quoted speech or thought.

examples.reading: ともだち と はなします。

questions.explanation: 母と means ‘with my mother’.

questions.sentence: パンと牛乳を買います。
questions.explanation: と gives a complete list: bread and milk.
と marks the exact words that were said.

lessons.title: Direction with へ
lessons.summary: へ emphasises movement toward a direction or destination. As a particle it is pronounced え.

examples.reading: にほん へ いきます。

questions.prompt: Which particle emphasises direction toward Tokyo?
questions.explanation: へ points the movement toward Tokyo.
The character is written へ but the particle is pronounced え.
へ marks the direction of returning.

lessons.title: From から to まで
lessons.summary: から marks a starting point and まで marks an ending point in time or space.

examples.japanese: 九時から五時まで働きます。
examples.reading: くじ から ごじ まで はたらきます。
examples.english: I work from nine until five.

questions.explanation: から marks Monday as the starting point.
まで marks the station as the end point.
The start takes から and the end takes まで.

lessons.title: Choosing に or で
lessons.summary: Use に for where something exists; use で for where an action happens.

examples.japanese: 公園に猫がいます。公園で子供が遊びます。
examples.reading: こうえん に ねこ が います。こうえん で こども が あそびます。
examples.english: There is a cat in the park. Children play in the park.
chunks: 公園に = exists in the park
公園で = acts in the park

questions.prompt: A teacher exists at school. Which particle fits?
questions.explanation: います describes existence, so the location takes に.

questions.prompt: A teacher teaches at school. Which particle fits?
questions.explanation: Teaching is an action happening at school, so use で.

questions.sentence: 机に本があります。机で勉強します。
choices: に marks existence; で marks action
に marks action; で marks existence
Both always mean the same thing
questions.answer: に marks existence; で marks action
questions.explanation: Choose the particle by the role of the place, not by translating English ‘at’.

lessons.title: Choosing は or が
lessons.summary: は establishes or contrasts a topic. が identifies or focuses the subject, especially new information.

examples.japanese: だれが先生ですか。田中さんが先生です。田中さんは親切です。
examples.reading: だれ が せんせい です か。たなかさん が せんせい です。たなかさん は しんせつ です。
examples.english: Who is the teacher? Mr Tanaka is the teacher. As for Mr Tanaka, he is kind.
chunks: 田中さんは = as for Mr Tanaka

questions.prompt: Which particle answers the focused question ‘Who did it?’
questions.explanation: が identifies Aiko as the specific answer to ‘who?’

questions.prompt: Which particle introduces dogs as the continuing topic?
questions.sentence: 犬＿かわいいです。犬は頭もいいです。
questions.explanation: は establishes dogs as what the following comments are about.

questions.sentence: コーヒー＿飲みますが、お茶は飲みません。
questions.explanation: は can contrast coffee with tea: coffee I drink, but tea I do not.
